simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to מֵצַר (H4712) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: מֵצַר (mêtsar) means something tight , i.e. (figuratively) trouble First listed occurrence: Lam 1 3.

definitions.full: H4712. metsar מֵצַר noun [masculine] straits, distress ; — absolute קָרָאתִי הַמֵּצַר מִןֿ Psa 118:5 ; plural הַמְּצָרִים Lam 1:3 the distresses , of conquered Judah; construct שְׁאוֺל מְצָרֵי Psa 116:3 the straits of Sheol, i.e. the worst possible (|| חֶבְלֵימָֿוֶת ).
